already-have.reason: Not implemented and not contradicted by any owner decision. The repo has no shunt, no current-sense element, no ADC driver, and no ADC attribution in GTZC: `secure/src/board/pq1.rs:295-296` defines `USB_VBUS_SENSE` (PA9) as a digital presence line only; `grep -rniE "shunt|current.?sense|INA2[12]9|\bADC\b"` over secure/src and docs hits only SCA bench-rig text (`docs/security/red-teaming.md:99-104`, `docs/verification/security-tooling-sota-2026-06.md:243`) and Trezor's TAMP ITAMP7/12/13 ADC-watchdog description in `docs/architecture/trezor-comparison.md:357`; `secure/src/sau.rs` secures AES/HASH/RNG/PKA/SAES, I2C1/2/4, UCPD1, TIM2/TIM3 but no ADC. `docs/hardware/hardware_requirements.md:100-112` lists tamper mesh / case switch / EMI can / rail filtering, no current sensing. No GitHub issue tracks power-budget attestation (searches: "current sense", "shunt", "ADC", "power budget", "implant", "hardware trojan" return nothing relevant; #249/#68/#67 are provisioning/transparency-log attestation, not runtime power sensing). The owner decision that exists is supportive, not contradictory: `hardware_requirements.md:139-150,196` fixes "no coin-cell battery, supercap on VBAT, sealed-for-life BOM", which is exactly the structural premise the proposal relies on.
already-have.corrections: (1) Pin feasibility: the proposal's "PA10 or PA6 if the mask moves" is half wrong. On STM32U585 PA10, PC13 and PB4 (the three `FREE_PINS`, `pq1.rs:345`) carry no ADC channel; the only bonded free-ish analog pad is PA6 (ADC1_IN11), which the consumption mask took on 2026-09-01 (`pq1.rs:301-318`, TIM3_CH1/AF2). The mask can relocate to PB4 (TIM3_CH1 AF2, bonded, NC) to free PA6 — or use an I2C current monitor (INA226-class) on a SECURE bus (I2C1/I2C4 are secured in `sau.rs`; I2C2 is the NS-reserved aux bus) and avoid the analog pin entirely, at the cost of a sensor that is itself a spoofable part unless it sits on the main PCB. (2) GTZC delta: ADC1/ADC4 are not attributed SECURE today; the proposal's requirement must add that bit to `sau::configure_gtzc` under the existing exact-equality `const assert!` pattern. (3) Energy-source nuance: pq1 is coin-cell-free but does carry a 0.47–1 F VBAT supercap (`hardware_requirements.md:139-150`); it is a second tap point an implant could draw from, though at ~3–5 J it cannot sustain a radio, so the shunt-at-VBUS-input argument stands if the supercap charge path is also downstream of the shunt. (4) The AW35602 USB port-protection IC (`evt-silicon-validation.md:231`, FLAGB on PB10, currently unread) sits at the VBUS input; whether it exposes a current-limit/monitor output is worth checking before adding a discrete shunt. (5) Related but distinct open work: the consumption mask's dilution is unmeasured on both boards (`evt-silicon-validation.md` §9) — a factory per-unit quiescent measurement would share that bench setup. No issue exists; one should be opened if pursued.

feasible.reason: The mechanism survives on pq1: the schematic (docs/hardware/schematics/AL_A66_MB_V10_20260826_1500.pdf, sheet 1 POWER + sheet 2 TYPE-C) shows a genuine single choke point — USB_VBUS → ET9555M OVP (U203) → VBUS → ET83101 buck (U105, L101 10 uH) → VDD3V6 → three NCP114 LDOs (VDD3V3 MCU, VDD1_3V3 both SEs gated by LDO2_EN/PA8, BOOT0) plus the AW99703 backlight boost and AW21036 RGB driver, which hang directly off VDD3V6. A shunt between the OVP output and the buck input is upstream of every rail an implant could tap, so the proposal's central claim is correct and it correctly flags kind=hardware. It is not a prevention: it raises cost. Three real bypasses must be stated and two parts of the written plan are wrong. (1) Measurement schedule: 'boot idle + seed wizard' is defeated by a sleep-aware implant. A PSM/eDRX-capable LTE module idles at microamps-to-low-mA and an nRF52-class BLE sniffer sleeps at microamps; the implant logs the display SPI/I2C during the wizard and transmits later. The claim that 'radio TX bursts are the loudest moment' during the wizard assumes a naive implant. Fix: continuous sampling whenever VBUS is present using the ADC analog watchdog (hardware threshold interrupt, no CPU polling) so any TX burst of tens-hundreds of mA lasting ms trips it; keep the boot-idle read as the calibrated baseline check. (2) Sense-chain spoofing: the rationale that spoofing is 'only possible when the sense element is downstream of or inside the tampered subassembly' is wrong — the Ledger implant was itself a main-board front-side mod; an implant on this board can equally pad/clamp the single analog sense line or swap the amp. The real value is that the attacker must additionally defeat the sense chain, which the SWD/RDP-0 + photo ceremony has to catch; say 'raises cost', not 'forces'. (3) Anything between the USB-C receptacle and the shunt (connector-swap implants, the OVP chip's footprint) is unmeasured; the shunt must sit at the connector-side node and the residual be documented. Self-powered implants are already deferred to D-08. (4) Pin claim 'PA10 or PA6' is half wrong: on STM32U585 only PA6 (ADC1_IN11) of the free pads {PA6, PA10, PC13, PB4} has any ADC function — PA10, PC13 and PB4 have none. PA6 is currently the production-mandatory consumption-mask output (TIM3_CH1/AF2, secure/src/board/pq1.rs:301-320) and is NC on the board (pin table PIN 16), so the EVT spin must both route PA6 and move the mask to PB4 (also TIM3_CH1/AF2 — same timer, same channel, trivial) or PA10 (TIM1_CH3). (5) Resolution/common-mode: a 50-100 mOhm high-side shunt on a ~5 V VBUS node cannot be read directly by the 3.3 V-referenced ADC (common mode out of range; 1 LSB at 12 bits = 0.8 mV = 8-16 mA), so a high-side current-sense amplifier (INA180/INA199 class, 26 V common mode) is mandatory; the U5's internal OPAMP2 cannot be used because its VINP/VINM/VOUT pads (PA6/PA7/PB0) are the LCD MOSI/DC. Alternatively an INA226 on the already-secured I2C2 aux bus (PB13/PB14, shared with the backlight and RGB drivers, SAU-reserved from NS) needs no ADC pin at all and also measures bus voltage. (6) Band normalisation: buck input current scales with 1/VBUS, and USB VBUS is spec'd 4.45-5.25 V, so a current-only band carries ~±9 % error before the implant is counted; either measure VBUS (INA226 route) or accept the widened band. Also read the baseline with the backlight and RGB driver OFF (LCM_EN/RGB_EN low) and the SE rail off (which is the reset default via R130), not 'backlight at a fixed brightness' — LED Vf and boost efficiency drift with temperature. Expected detector floor after these corrections is ~2-5 mA at the input node against a ~25-45 mA MCU+buck+LDO quiescent with per-unit calibration, which catches any radio in active/idle-connected states and an MCU sniffer that is awake, and misses PSM-parked modems and passive taps (D-02). Cost M is right only if it includes the amp/INA, EVT re-spin, factory calibration write (per-unit value in OTP or a flash page at the RDP-0 ceremony, verifiable over SWD), and a GTZC change. Priority P1 is optimistic for a cost-raiser with three stated bypasses; P2 is more honest, but not 'wildly wrong'.
feasible.corrections: 1. Replace the 'boot idle + seed wizard' schedule with continuous ADC analog-watchdog monitoring whenever VBUS is present (hardware threshold, DMA/IRQ, no polling); keep a calibrated quiescent read at boot with LCM_EN, RGB_EN and LDO2_EN all low. 2. State the detector targets awake radios/MCUs; PSM-parked LTE, sleeping BLE SoCs and passive taps are below the floor (D-02, D-08 cover those). 3. Rewrite the rationale: the shunt raises attacker cost by forcing an additional sense-chain modification on the main board; it does not make telemetry spoofing impossible (Ledger's implant was a main-board mod). 4. Place the shunt at the USB-C receptacle-side VBUS node (before the ET9555M OVP, or immediately after it with the OVP footprint inside the verified photo set); document that the connector itself is unmeasured. 5. Pins: only PA6 (ADC1_IN11) is analog-capable among the free pads; PA10/PC13/PB4 have no ADC. Route PA6 on the EVT spin and move the consumption mask to PB4 (TIM3_CH1/AF2, same timer) or PA10 (TIM1_CH3). 6. Add a high-side current-sense amplifier (INA180/INA199) — the ADC cannot read a 5 V common-mode shunt directly and 12-bit/0.8 mV LSB is 8-16 mA per LSB without gain; or use an INA226 on the secured I2C2 aux bus (no ADC pin, bus voltage included). 7. Normalise for VBUS voltage (4.45-5.25 V spec) or widen the band ~±9 %; prefer measuring power. 8. GTZC: ADC12 is GTZC1_TZSC_SECCFGR3 bit 8 (not ADC4, which lives in GTZC2 and the firmware never configures); add it to the exact-equality const assert in secure/src/sau.rs. 9. Per-unit baseline: write at the RDP-0 ceremony into OTP or a per-device flash page so the SWD verifier can check it against the BOM-derived band; the supercap (CPH3225A on VBAT) cannot hold it. 10. Priority P2 rather than P1; cost M must include amp/INA, re-spin, calibration step and firmware.

vendor-claim.reason: Precedent and novelty claims hold up against the code and the cited sources. (1) 'none shipped' — Trezor: the only current/power measurement in /home/nicola/repos/trezor-firmware (HEAD 6ab39e95, 2026-10-07) is the T3W1 npm1300 PMIC path (core/embed/io/power_manager/npm1300/power_monitoring.c, npm1300.c:701-714, inc/io/pmic.h:36-57 `ibat`, `ntc_disconnected`, `battery_disconnected`). Its consumers are battery/charging logic and telemetry only: power_manager_poll.c:78-145 EMA 'jump' detectors feed `telemetry_batt_errors_t` (core/embed/sec/telemetry/inc/sec/telemetry.h) and the prodtest welcome screen (core/embed/rust/src/ui/layout_eckhart/prodtest/welcome.rs:128-135); no path refuses signing, halts, or triggers tamper on an out-of-band current. Trezor's tamper driver (core/embed/sec/tamper/stm32u5/tamper.c) enables internal TAMP sources + PWR->BDCR1 MONEN (voltage monitor), not a shunt/ADC current band. The grep hit 'Read the current sensor reversible configuration' (prodtest_tropic.c:3281) is a wording trap — 'current' = present; it reads TROPIC01's internal sensor config bits, not a current sensor. Ledger: Grand's slides (hardwear.io USA 2026, 'LEDGER RESPONSE') list only 'Check hardware integrity against known-good pictures' and 'looking into further hardening'; news.bitcoin.com (2026-10-10) quotes Ledger as 'working on further, enhanced anti-tampering solutions' with no detail. No web evidence that Ledger, Trezor, Coldcard, BitBox, Keystone, Passport or GridPlus ships on-board current-budget attestation. (2) Cited academic numbers are accurate: the Piliposyan & Khursheed paper (DOI 10.1109/TC.2022.3230877, IEEE TC) uses INA219 high-side sensors with 12-bit ADC at '1mW resolution', OC-SVM 'F1-score = 0.997 at 50mW', LOF 'F1-score = 0.88 at 5mW', and states 'ultra-low power passive Trojans, e.g. resistors and capacitors, should be addressed by other techniques such as visual inspection'. (3) Grand slides 'FRONT-SIDE MODIFICATIONS' verbatim: 'Battery has reduced size in order to fit implant', 'Fixed 10k resistor replaces NTC thermistor from original battery', 'Fuel gauge resistor bypassed to always appear 100% full'; implant = MCU + eSIM + cellular modem tapping the OLED SPI bus, 'transmits over 4G LTE'. (4) repo_evidence verified: secure/src/board/pq1.rs:296 `USB_VBUS_SENSE` PA9 digital-only; pq1.rs:45 'PA6, PA10, PC13 are the free pins'; docs/hardware/hardware_requirements.md:98-112 lists mesh/case switch/EMI can/rail filtering, no current sensing; grep for ADC/shunt/INA/current-sense across secure/src/hw and docs/hardware returns nothing (docs/security/red-teaming.md:99,104 mention a shunt only as the SCA analyst's probe).
vendor-claim.corrections: Minor precision fixes, none disqualifying: (a) The slides do NOT state the motive 'because it was power-visible'; they state the battery was shrunk to fit the implant and the gauge resistor bypassed to read 100% — the causal reading (hiding reduced capacity / implant draw from the fuel gauge) is a reasonable inference, so phrase it as inference. The news.bitcoin.com source only confirms an implant existed and Ledger's response; it does not support the telemetry-spoofing detail — attribute that solely to the Grand slides. (b) The 5 mW figure is LOF-specific (0.88); OC-SVM peaks at 82.6% at 5 mW — state 'LOF 0.88' to be exact. The paper also notes its own setup is 'oblivious' to Trojans powered from legitimate ICs' I/O pins unless each IC is individually monitored; a single upstream VBUS shunt as proposed does cover I/O-powered implants (all energy still crosses it), which is a genuine advantage worth stating. (c) Nearest vendor precedent to name: Trezor T3W1's npm1300 PMIC measures `ibat`/`vbus` but uses it only for charging, fuel-gauge sanity (NTC/battery disconnected, 5 °C / 500 mV jump flags) and telemetry — a 'measured but not security-gated' precedent, i.e. the sensing hardware exists at a competitor but the attestation use does not. (d) Broader non-wallet prior art exists and should be cited for completeness: PDN-impedance anomaly sensing (PDNPulse, arXiv 2204.02482) and the ACM survey 'From ICs to Device: A Survey on Hardware Tampering Detection via Power Delivery Network and Signal Trace' (doi 10.1145/3779441); novelty stays 'beyond' relative to hardware-wallet vendors but is 'application of published method' relative to academia. (e) Ledger LSB-006 (2019) is the inverse precedent: a shunt in the USB path used by the ATTACKER for OLED power analysis — relevant to D-03's design because the same shunt node is an SCA observation point; keep the sense amplifier output S-world-only and consider that the shunt adds measurable series impedance for an external observer.
